title: Preflight tokenization shim with session-aware dedupe and SIMD-normalization
creator: Ariana Chen
description:
Goal: reduce prefill-side CPU overhead and wall-clock latency for short and mid-length prompts by introducing a lightweight preflight tokenization shim that does session-aware deduplication, SIMD-aligned UTF8 normalization, and a tiny LRU hint cache for recurring system prefixes. Motivation: upstream kernel-selection and attention scheduling improvements are limited by preprocessing jitter—we see 15-25% end-to-end token-per-second loss on 4–32 token prefixes due to per-request normalization and hash computation. This ticket implements a minimal, low-risk shim that runs before the full tokenizer pipeline and exposes hints to the runtime so later stages can skip redundant work and select narrower kernels for common cases.

Scope and non-goals: implement shim and in-process LRU hint cache, add deterministic unit and perf tests, wire shim to runtime cost hints interface. Do NOT replace the existing tokenizer or change model-facing token ids. Maintain byte-for-byte tokenization equivalence to the canonical tokenizer. Do NOT attempt to offload to GPU in this ticket.

Acceptance criteria:
- CPU microbench: preflight shim reduces per-request preprocessing CPU cycles by >=18% on 8-token average prompts in our CI microbench.
- Latency p99 improvement: p99 prefill latency reduced by >=12% for short prompts in the regional perf cluster.
- No change to generated token sequences for canonical tests (tokenization equivalence tests pass).
- Runtime integration: shim exposes 1-byte hint flags and a 64-bit prefix hash to the kernel selection path; runtime path uses hints to prioritize narrow attention kernels for single-session short prefixes.
- Observability: add Prometheus counters for cache hit/miss, normalized-bytes, and dedupe-skipped-tokens; surfaced in Console under "Prefill preprocessing".
- Docs: short README in repo explaining shim semantics and knob controls.

Implementation plan:
1) Design: finalize in-memory LRU layout optimized for 64-bit prefix hashes and per-session namespaces (2 days).
2) PoC: implement shim in C++ runtime with SIMD UTF8 normalization using existing simd helpers (3 days).
3) Tests: deterministic tokenization comparison suite + fuzz harness for malformed utf8 (2 days).
4) Integration: expose hint API to kernel selector and add unit tests in runtime-optimizer (2 days).
5) Benchmarks and rollout: run canary in staging with 10% traffic, monitor metrics, then full rollout if thresholds met (3 days).

Risks and mitigations:
- Hash collisions causing incorrect dedupe: use 64-bit hash and verify deterministic fallback to canonical tokenizer when in doubt. Add mismatch alerting.
- SIMD normalization subtle differences across architectures: include architecture-specific test vectors and fallback scalar path.
- Memory blow-up for high-session cardinality: per-session LRU capped and eviction policy tuned by env var.

Notes for reviewers: this approach favors small, audit-friendly changes over large tokenizer rewrites. It enables kernel selector to make earlier decisions and reduces CPU variance for high-QPS short-chat workloads.
